# Caching

When a cache earns its place, and — more often — when it does not.

5 unit(s). `Stages` is the maturity range where a concept applies — an agent filters on it so that concepts from a larger system than yours are not offered.

| Concept | Stages | Cost | What it is |
| :-- | :-- | --: | :-- |
| [Cache-Aside](cache-aside.md) | 2,3,4,5 | 1 | The default caching pattern: the application checks the cache, falls back to the origin on a miss, and populates the cache itself. |
| [Cache Sizing](cache-sizing.md) | 2,3,4,5 | 0 | Sizing a cache from its working set rather than from the total data volume, and computing what the cache actually relieves. |
| [Cache Stampede](cache-stampede.md) | 2,3,4,5 | 1 | When a popular cache entry expires, concurrent requests all miss simultaneously and overwhelm the origin with duplicate work. |
| [TTL and Invalidation](ttl-and-invalidation.md) | 2,3,4,5 | 0 | Choosing expiry from tolerable staleness, and treating the TTL as the backstop for the invalidation that was missed. |
| [When Not to Cache](when-not-to-cache.md) | 0,1,2,3,4,5 | 0 | The thresholds below which a cache adds a component, a failure mode, and a class of staleness bug in exchange for no measurable benefit. |

`Cost` is the complexity points a concept adds if adopted; 0 means it is a technique rather than a component. See `frameworks/complexity-budget/`.
